target_customer: Grocery and brick and mortar retailers that pay for shelf monitoring cameras and software to reduce out-of-stocks and labour
problem: Stores do not know in real time what is missing, misplaced or mispriced on shelves, causing lost sales and wasted labour on manual checks.
business_model: B2B hardware plus SaaS: shelf cameras with a software platform sold per store on subscription
product_category: Retail computer vision and shelf intelligence

founders.name: Francois Chaubard
founders.background_notes: YC page says he holds a Stanford PhD and wrote AI for Retail. Wellfound (seen in a search summary) cites a Stanford computer vision background.

founders.name: Michael Cantalino
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the YC page and named in the Uncork Capital welcome post.

founders.name: Adriano Quiroga
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the YC page and named in the Uncork Capital welcome post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Deep learning computer vision to recognise every product on shelves from low cost cameras in varied store conditions needed large labelled image sets and custom hardware, difficult for a small team in 2016.

defensibility.rationale: Large labelled shelf image data and deep store workflow integrations are hard to copy, but shelf scanning by robots and fixed cameras attracted several funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Walmart's robot pilot with Bossa Nova ended after about 500 of a planned 1000 deployments (ABI Research), while Focal later won a chainwide Walmart Canada deployment after a 70 store pilot (2022); no acquirer bought Focal in sources found.

market_need_then: Out-of-stocks are a known retail problem; the Uncork Capital welcome post describes grocery chains in the Bay Area using the early Focal product, but no dated 2016 demand figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses focal.systems, a vanity domain suffix, rather than a .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise retail technology: Real-Time Shelf Insights And Automation

branding.brand_signature: FocalOS, branded as the operating system of retail
branding.community_and_virality: Awards (Retail Systems Awards 2026, Confluent Data Streaming Startup of the Year) are cited on its site; no consumer community since it sells to retailers.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within grocery technology but the name is shared with Focal audio and other firms, and sources show no brand driven growth.

pivots.from: Focal Tablet attached to shopping carts with in-store navigation and out-of-stock detection
pivots.to: Fixed shelf cameras and FocalOS shelf intelligence
pivots.why: Not stated in sources opened; the cart device is described in an Uncork Capital welcome post (undated page) and the current product is shelf cameras.

outcome_analysis: Focal started with a cart mounted tablet and moved to fixed shelf cameras and software, winning large retailers including Walmart Canada after a 2022 pilot and Wakefern, Village Super Market and Asda trials. It raised a 25.8 million dollar Series B led by Point72 in late 2021 and shows no sign of exit or shutdown, though retail sales cycles are slow and robot rivals such as Simbe compete.
notes: Series B date is December 2021 per CB Insights and November 2021 per VCBacked (aggregators); the CDO Magazine page I opened shows only a July 2023 update date. Aggregators also list a Series A of about 8.5M to 9M in 2017 with Costanoa and a total near 37M, unverified and not recorded as a round; the Series B alone is 25.8M so earlier rounds are missing. The Uncork Capital post names Amazon Go as the main competitor but its page metadata shows 2026 so it is undated and not used as a dated competitor source; Bossa Nova robots at Walmart began in 2016 per ABI Research but no source ties them to Focal at founding. Founded year 2016 follows the YC listing as seen in a search summary. Layoff and shutdown search found no reports.
